task_instance: Deploy a real-time SageMaker endpoint for an embedding model (TEI, BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5) using the skill's deploy.py with production defaults (autoscaling target-tracking policy, 3 CloudWatch alarms, resource tagging), then smoke-test it with invoke_endpoint.py and tear it down with teardown.py.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is creating live AWS SageMaker resources (Model, EndpointConfig, Endpoint, Application Auto Scaling target/policy, CloudWatch alarms) via boto3/aws-cli calls such as create_model, create_endpoint_config, create_endpoint, put-scaling-policy, and put-metric-alarm. This inherently requires: (1) a real AWS account with SageMaker/CloudWatch/Application-Auto-Scaling/IAM/S3 access, (2) a usable IAM execution role and S3 bucket (upstream skill dependencies hf-cloud-sagemaker-iam-preflight / an account-controlled bucket), and (3) provisioning billed compute (e.g. ml.g5.xlarge GPU or ml.c6i.2xlarge CPU instance) that runs until torn down. The sandbox has no `aws` CLI installed and only proxy-injected placeholder AWS credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = 'proxy-injected', not tied to any real account), so `aws sts get-caller-identity` cannot resolve an identity and no SageMaker API call could succeed. Even if credentials existed, actually creating the endpoint would be a paid, account-bound cloud resource, which the task's safety rules explicitly forbid ('no account-bound or paid services'). The skill's own scripts/ directory (deploy.py, deploy_ic.py, deploy_async.py, invoke_endpoint.py, teardown.py) is also not present in the skill folder as shipped (only SKILL.md and LICENSE), consistent with the doc's own note that some harnesses install only SKILL.md and the scripts must be fetched from the source repo -- but fetching/writing those scripts was moot once the fundamental blocker (no AWS account/credentials, and a policy against paid/account-bound services) was hit. I did not attempt to write substitute deploy/teardown scripts and run them against a mocked or local SageMaker, since the skill's stated core intent is specifically to create and verify a real, working AWS-hosted production endpoint (InService status, real invocation, CloudWatch log scan) -- a mocked run would not exercise or validate that deliverable.
evidence: Read SKILL.md in full (references AWS SageMaker create_endpoint workflow, IAM roles, S3 model artifacts, CloudWatch alarms, Application Auto Scaling). Checked repo contents: `find .../huggingface__skills__hf-cloud-sagemaker-production-defaults -type f` returned only SKILL.md and LICENSE (no scripts/ directory shipped). Checked tooling: `which aws` -> not found (exit 127); `env | grep -i aws` showed only AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=proxy-injected and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=proxy-injected (not real credentials); `aws sts get-caller-identity` failed because the aws CLI itself is not installed. No SageMaker/IAM/CloudWatch/S3 resources were created or attempted beyond this diagnostic check, per the safety rule against paid or account-bound services.
